title: Individual safety work: women ridesharing drivers’ responses to sexual harassment on the job
abstract: Research has studied the various ways in which women respond to sexual harassment in the workplace, including pursuing legal and organizational avenues of redress to prevent future attacks. However, in the gig-based, ridesharing industry, these techniques might not be possible. Ridesharing involves all those services whereby passengers request a ride from one location to another, usually through an app on their mobile phone. This study explores what women must often do on their own to protect themselves from future sexual harassment, or what I call ‘individual safety work’, of 44 mostly women ridesharing drivers operating in the United States. Using qualitative content analysis methods, I find that women respond to sexual harassment by implementing three primary, personally based strategies after being victimized in their jobs as drivers: implementing service changes; purchasing self-protection equipment or changing the seating of passengers/making physical alterations to their automobiles to guard themselves; and relying on interpersonal defence mechanisms.
